C-01.1.answer: A missing or malformed archive summary refuses on read (LEDGER_ARCHIVE_BROKEN) — never read as zero settled. The gate's total lives in that hot summary and never reads cold, so a lost cold segment cannot read as freed cap: it leaves the total unchanged and is caught by sakk ledger verify, not silently treated as no spend.
C-01.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a corrupt archive summary refuses; a lost segment fails verify, never freeing cap

C-01.2.answer: The test drops a field from the summary and asserts the next read refuses, then removes a sealed segment and asserts the gate's total is unchanged (no freed cap) while verify fails — so a missing input is never the quiet success of a lower total.
C-01.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a corrupt archive summary refuses; a lost segment fails verify, never freeing cap

C-02.1.answer: The segments and shards are enumerated from archive.segments and from sha256(callId)'s first two hex, never a hand-written list; the single rule 'seal the oldest settled when hot settled reaches SEAL_AT' is applied in one place that settle calls, and totals read the summary the same way everywhere.
C-02.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::totals equal a flat ledger of the same calls, hot and cold

C-02.2.answer: The same summary is the single source for totalsOf, reserve's cap check and status; reserve, settle and status all go through it, and readLedger migrates a v2 ledger to v3 on first write so an old book is not a second code path.
C-02.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a v2 ledger still reads, settles and seals after migration

C-03.1.answer: The tamper tests put the bug back: a flipped byte in a sealed segment, a re-linked prev, and a wrong archive.tip each make sakk ledger verify (and the per-call tip check) go red; removing the tamper makes it green, so the check fails for that reason and only that.
C-03.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::verify catches a flipped byte, a broken link and a wrong tip

C-03.2.answer: The crash-replay test really interrupts a seal between the segment write, the index write and the hot commit (by invoking the seal steps directly and stopping between them), then runs a real read and reserve, so it observes recovery, not a mock of it.
C-03.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a seal interrupted before the hot commit is a redoable prefix, no entry lost

C-03.3.answer: The per-call tip check compares archive.tip against sha256 of the actual last segment on disk, not a stored flag, so it fails when the segment is missing or changed, not only when a record is absent; verify walks the real chain end to end.
C-03.3.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::verify catches a flipped byte, a broken link and a wrong tip

C-04.1.answer: Per call the work is bounded by the hot size (outstanding capped at MAX_INFLIGHT=10,000) plus one index shard and at most one segment read on a settle of an archived id; a seal touches one segment and the shards of its SEAL_AT ids. The bound is asserted by counting file reads/entries scanned, never a stopwatch, and a ledger of 100k settled calls is shown to cost the same per call as 1k.
C-04.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::per-call work stays flat as history grows (operation count, not a clock)

C-05.1.answer: Each spec sentence has a test: hot-only reads for the gate decision, seal at SEAL_AT, tip-only per-call verification, the full-chain verify, and export rebuilding a flat ledger — a test fails if any is not kept.
C-05.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::the spec's claims each have a test that fails without them

C-05.2.answer: status and --json totals are the cold summary plus hot, checked equal to a flat recomputation; sakk ledger verify exits non-zero on a broken chain and zero on a sound one, and export writes a file that reads back as one valid ledger with the same totals.
C-05.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::export rebuilds one valid ledger with the same totals; verify's exit code is acted on

C-06.1.answer: The README's per-call figures (2万→96ms, 10万→539ms) are the pre-fix measurement, shown as the problem that motivated the split, not a post-fix benchmark claim; the flatness it promises is backed by the structural test (the gate reads only the hot file, zero cold reads), not by a number, and verify/export are backed by their own tests.
C-06.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::per-call work stays flat as history grows (operation count, not a clock)

C-07.1.answer: The cold segments and index shards are repository files an operator could hand-edit; they are never trusted blindly — the chain hash and the tip check detect a changed or lost segment, and the gate's go/no-go uses the hot file's atomic summary, not a figure recomputed from untrusted cold entries.
C-07.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::verify catches a flipped byte, a broken link and a wrong tip

C-07.2.answer: Archiving never settles or clears anything: a reconciliation-required entry stays in hot until a person clears it, and an archived SETTLED entry is read only to compare a re-settle for idempotency, so the agent cannot use the cold path to clear what only a person may.
C-07.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a reconciliation entry is never sealed; re-settling an archived id checks the amount

C-08.1.answer: The cold and index directories derive from the ledger file's already-canonical path (the same symlink/hard-link-free canonicalization reserve uses), so one ledger has exactly one cold trail and one index, reachable by one name.
C-08.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::the cold and index paths are canonical, one per ledger

C-09.1.answer: The read path is tried with no cold directory (a fresh v3), with a v2 ledger that must migrate, mid-seal crash states, and a sound multi-segment history, so the states a real run reaches are each exercised, not only the happy one.
C-09.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a v2 ledger still reads, settles and seals after migration

C-09.2.answer: The tests drive the real reserve/settle/seal through the library and through bin/sakk.mjs status/verify/export, so the archive fires on the path a caller and the CLI actually take, not only in a unit stub.
C-09.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::export rebuilds one valid ledger with the same totals; verify's exit code is acted on

C-10.1.answer: The seal is a step inside settle, run under the lock, not a rule in a doc; a test fails if settled entries in hot ever exceed SEAL_AT after a settle, so the step cannot be quietly dropped.
C-10.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::settling past the seal threshold always seals, never leaves hot unbounded

C-10.2.answer: Every mutation (reserve, settle, halt, reconcile) goes through readLedger+lock, and migration happens on the first write through that path, so there is no second route that writes the books without sealing or without the summary; what the gate read is the hot file it just locked.
C-10.2.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::settling past the seal threshold always seals, never leaves hot unbounded

C-11.1.answer: archive.settledUsd and archive.tip are confirmed running state: only the seal step, under the lock, adds a segment's actuals to settledUsd and advances the tip, and only after the segment and its shards are on disk, so the summary's meaning never outruns what is sealed.
C-11.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::a seal interrupted before the hot commit is a redoable prefix, no entry lost

C-15.1.answer: The tests use real segment files, real index shards and the real recovery on a real interrupted seal — no stand-in that writes its own evidence; the per-call cost test seals a real 100k-entry history.
C-15.1.guard: test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::per-call work stays flat as history grows (operation count, not a clock)
